signals.signal: Branch network cut to 334 units at 30/06/2026, from 347 at 31/12/2025 and 357 at 30/06/2025 (-23 YoY, -13 in six months). Longer arc from the FY2025 Board report: 388 branches at end-2024 to 347 at end-2025 (-41 in one year). BoD wording: the physical network 'continued to be optimized to meet client needs'.
signals.source_name: BRD Half Year Report (Board of Directors Report) June 2026, section 3 'Commercial activity' and network table; BRD Annual Report 2025 (BVB filing 18/03/2026)
signals.implies: Sustained branch contraction with no let-up: 41 closures in 2025 and 13 more in H1-2026. Every closed branch pushes cash-in/cash-out volume onto the surviving sites and onto off-site devices - the core business case for cash recyclers (TCRs, machines that take a deposited note and re-dispense it, cutting cash-in-transit trips) and unmanned 24/7 cash pods.
signals.likelihood: Very likely to continue through H2-2026
signals.followup: Ask BRD which sites close in H2-2026 and whether closed locations are being replaced by unmanned self-service points rather than abandoned.

signals.signal: 24-hour self-service capability for CASH transactions available in 268 branches at 30/06/2026, up from 266 branches at 31/03/2026 (both figures from BRD's own interim reports). That is 268 of 334 branches - roughly 80% of the network - with a 24/7 cash zone.
signals.source_name: BRD 2Q/H1 2026 Results Presentation slide 'And a leaner, optimised network' + BRD Half Year Report June 2026; BRD Q1 2026 Quarterly Report (BVB, 29/04/2026) for the 266 figure
signals.implies: The zone rollout is nearly saturated - only ~66 branches lack one, and it is growing at just 2 per quarter. The value has shifted from NEW zones to UPGRADING existing ones: withdrawal-only ATMs replaced by deposit/recycling machines, plus managed services (remote monitoring, cash forecasting, first- and second-line maintenance) across a fleet that is now the bank's primary cash channel.
signals.likelihood: High - upgrade cycle is the realistic 6-12 month opportunity, not new-zone build
signals.followup: Establish how many of the 268 zones are withdrawal-only versus deposit-capable, and the age and OEM of the installed base - this is the single highest-value unknown at BRD.

signals.signal: Total investments of RON 118 million at Group level and RON 112 million at Bank level in H1-2026, against approximately RON 100 million for both in H1-2025 (roughly +18% YoY). No capitalised research and development expenditure.
signals.source_name: BRD Half Year Report June 2026, 'Financial position - assets' (tangible and intangible assets note)
signals.implies: A concrete and growing capex envelope of roughly RON 236m annualised (c.EUR 46m). That is a fraction of Banca Transilvania's RON 1,017.40m 2026 investment budget, so BRD is far more likely to buy self-service capacity as a managed service or operating lease than as outright capex.
signals.followup: Lead with a fixed-fee, no-capex device-as-a-service model (the structure Payten used at Banca Intesa Beograd) rather than a hardware purchase proposal.

signals.signal: Cost programme explicitly trading people and property for technology: staff expenses -8.3% YoY in H1-2026 and -10.5% YoY in Q2-2026; costs excluding turnover tax and the prior-year guarantee/resolution fund contribution -3% YoY; management attributes this to 'operating model optimisation through network resizing, process simplification and organisational streamlining' and 'reduced real estate footprint costs'. Other expenses rose on IT&C costs from 'depreciation of past investments and ongoing infrastructure and digitalization initiatives'. Cost/income improved to 49.6% from 50.7%. Turnover tax doubled to RON 139m from RON 66m (4% rate versus 2%).
signals.source_name: BRD 2Q/H1 2026 Results Presentation, operating expenses slide; BRD Half Year Report June 2026
signals.implies: Management has publicly committed to substituting technology for headcount and floor space, while a doubled turnover tax squeezes the P&L. That is the exact economic setup a recycler-plus-managed-services proposition monetises: fewer tellers per branch, teller cash handling moved into the machine, smaller branch footprint.
signals.likelihood: High - stated and quantified management intent
signals.followup: Frame the ROI in FTE-equivalents and square metres saved per branch, not in device price - that is the language BRD's own disclosure uses.

signals.signal: Group active headcount fell to 5,124 at 31/12/2025 from 5,840 at 31/12/2024 (-716, -12.3%); Bank active headcount 4,965 versus 5,670. Group average active headcount 5,458 in 2025 versus 5,912 in 2024. 'Active employees' are full-time staff excluding maternity and long-term sick leave.
signals.source_name: BRD Annual Report 2025 - audited IFRS financial statements, employee note (filed with BVB 18/03/2026)
signals.implies: A 12% workforce cut in a single year, alongside 41 branch closures, means surviving branches must run with materially fewer tellers. Automating the cash desk is the only way to hold service levels - a direct, quantified opening for cash automation and assisted self-service.
signals.followup: Pull the 30/06/2026 headcount from the H1 interim financial statements to size the 2026 reduction and convert it into a per-branch teller number.

signals.signal: BRD's own website states the bank has 'aproximativ 1.400 de ATM-uri' (approximately 1,400 ATMs). BRD also publishes a contactless-terminal list on brd.ro that distinguishes two device classes - 'ATM' and 'MBA' (Masina Bancara Automata, the in-branch self-service machine used for cash deposit and bill payment) - confirming a separate deposit-capable estate alongside the cash-out ATM fleet.
signals.source_name: BRD.ro - 'Tranzactii contactless la ATM-urile BRD' page and the linked 'Lista ATM-uri Contactless' PDF (both live and checked 30/07/2026)
signals.implies: Partially re-verifies the previously carried ~1,400 ATM figure directly on the bank's own site (the baseline had it unverified), and establishes MBA as a distinct deposit-capable device class. The MBA estate, not the cash-out ATMs, is the natural recycler-replacement target.
signals.followup: The ~1,400 figure is undated on the page, and no ATM/MBA split or OEM is published anywhere. Naming BRD's fleet OEM remains an open standing task - pursue via BRD directly, via CIT One, or via field observation of device fascias.

signals.signal: In Q2-2026 BRD 'strengthened its digital onboarding process by enabling the use of the new Electronic Identity Card (CEI) with chip for remote customer identification and application activation'. The results deck flags 'eID accepted for onboarding' as NEW. Alongside it: Click to Pay integrated for online card payments, RCA motor insurance purchase in-app, State Treasury payments with mandatory fiscal details, in-app card issuance and a new onboarding journey.
signals.source_name: BRD Half Year Report June 2026, commercial activity section; BRD 2Q/H1 2026 Results Presentation
signals.implies: Romania's new chip electronic ID is now live in a tier-1 bank's remote onboarding flow. This sets the reference standard every other Romanian bank will be measured against, and creates demand for chip/NFC document reading, liveness detection and identity verification plus the AML/KYC screening behind it.
signals.likelihood: High - peer banks (CEC, Raiffeisen RO, BT) will follow in 2026-2027
signals.followup: Identify BRD's eID/eKYC vendor (FintechOS and Backbase are the carried incumbents) and pitch the equivalent chip-eID capability to the peers that have not yet enabled it.

signals.signal: 178.2 million acquiring transactions processed in H1-2026 - disclosed and flagged as NEW in the results deck (BRD had not previously published acquiring scale). Click to Pay integrated in Q2-2026. BRD is one of only three original RoPay instant-payment banks (with Libra and CEC Bank) and has extended RoPay to e-commerce QR payments.
signals.source_name: BRD 2Q/H1 2026 Results Presentation, e-banking slide; BRD Half Year Report June 2026; RoPay participant page
signals.implies: First-time disclosure of acquiring volume signals that merchant acquiring has become a strategic reporting line. Volume of that order drives POS terminal estate renewal, softPOS, QR/RoPay acceptance at the terminal (which needs a terminal software refresh across the whole estate) and additional transaction-monitoring and fraud capacity.
signals.likelihood: High - RoPay QR at POS requires estate-wide terminal software work
signals.followup: Size BRD's installed POS terminal base and identify its terminal-management/estate-management vendor; the RoPay QR-at-POS rollout is a concrete, dated hook.

signals.entity: Safetech Innovations S.A. / unnamed Romanian beneficiary (the flagged BRD SOC renewal window)
signals.signal: Safetech Innovations announced on 22/07/2026 (current report 34/2026 to BVB and ASF) a significant contract - value exceeding 10% of its last annual total revenue - worth EUR 2,728,000 excluding VAT, running 36 months from signature, with a beneficiary described only as 'confidential; a Romanian entity unaffiliated with the Company'. Scope: (i) cybersecurity services, (ii) sale of its own cybersecurity monitoring solution, (iii) sale of other security solutions. The client is NOT named.
signals.source_name: Safetech Innovations S.A., Current Report 34/2026 (BVB / ASF filing, PDF)
signals.implies: A 36-month, monitoring-platform-led contract of this size landing weeks before the flagged ~Sep-2026 BRD SOC renewal window is consistent with that renewal being signed early - but the beneficiary is expressly confidential and must NOT be briefed as BRD. Either way it confirms the Romanian bank-SOC renewal cycle is live now, which is the entry point for security/HSM and transaction-monitoring cross-sell.
signals.likelihood: Renewal cycle active now; counterparty identity unconfirmed
signals.followup: Watch Safetech's H1-2026 report and any BRD supplier disclosure for confirmation of the counterparty. Do not present this as a BRD contract until confirmed.

signals.signal: The Safetech Innovations Global Services case-study page describing SOC (Security Operations Centre) services for BRD - Groupe Societe Generale now returns a 404 'Page not found'. The only surviving description of that engagement - a 3-year term from March 2020 with automatic renewal for a further 3 years, which is where the ~Sep-2026 renewal date came from - exists in search-engine snippets, not on any live page.
signals.implies: The public evidence base for the BRD-Safetech SOC relationship has been withdrawn. Removal of a named-client case study commonly accompanies a contract change or a client confidentiality request - consistent with a renegotiation in progress. The ~Sep-2026 renewal date should now be treated as UNVERIFIED from any live source.
signals.followup: Operator task: retrieve an archived (Wayback) copy of the case study to pin the original contract start and renewal dates before briefing anyone on the September window.

signals.entity: CIT One S.A. (BRD 33.33% joint venture with BCR and Raiffeisen Bank Romania)
signals.signal: BRD's audited 2025 statements list CIT One S.A. as a joint venture held 33.33%, activity 'Protectie, paza si transport numerar' (security, guarding and cash transport), registered at Splaiul Independentei 319L, Bucharest. The three-way equal shareholding by BCR, BRD and Raiffeisen was authorised by the Romanian Competition Council and announced on 01/10/2020, with the stated aim to 'optimise, develop and streamline cash transport and processing' and, per the joint statement, to pursue 'dezvoltarea accelerata a activitatii CIT ONE'.
signals.source_name: BRD Annual Report 2025 - IFRS financial statements, associates and joint ventures note (BVB, 18/03/2026); Revista Biz, 01/10/2020
signals.implies: Romania's three largest foreign-owned banks pool cash logistics and processing in one vehicle. Cash-cycle economics - CIT replenishment runs, cash forecasting, cash-centre processing - are therefore decided jointly, so a recycler business case at BRD is really a CIT One-wide business case. Selling cash-cycle optimisation software and managed services into CIT One reaches three banks at once.
signals.followup: Map CIT One's own cash-centre technology stack and whether it handles ATM/recycler replenishment for all three shareholders - this is a single, high-leverage target Printec has not addressed.

signals.signal: Digital migration close to complete on the transactional side: 1.96 million YOU BRD users at 30/06/2026 (+11% YoY); 22 million app transactions in H1-2026 (+21.8% YoY) worth RON 35.2 billion (+22.4% YoY); 80% of deposits opened in YOU BRD; 97% of corporate and 96% of SME transactions were digital; 1.2 million clients enrolled in the cashback programme with RON 4.8 million paid since June 2024; 275,000 written messages handled in H1-2026 (vs 270,000 in H1-2025); ~780,000 calls received, 98% handled (up from 95%), 85% answered within 20 seconds, 9-second average answer time down from 21 seconds.
signals.source_name: BRD 2Q/H1 2026 Results Presentation, e-banking slides; BRD Half Year Report June 2026
signals.implies: With 96-97% of business payments already digital, the branch is now almost purely a cash and advisory channel. That polarisation is the strongest single argument for replacing teller cash handling with recyclers and for keeping only unmanned 24/7 cash pods where branches close.
signals.followup: Use the 96-97% digital-corporate figure verbatim as the anchor in the branch-automation pitch to BRD and to its Romanian peers.

signals.signal: The Financial Supervisory Authority (ASF) Council sanctioned BRD - Groupe Societe Generale S.A., in its capacity as a credit-institution intermediary, with a fine of RON 67,100 among its June-2026 decisions. The identified issues concerned 'mecanismele organizatorice aferente protejarii drepturilor de proprietate a activelor clientilor, respectiv aspecte operationale si organizatorice privind fluxurile interne pentru activitatea de tranzactionare si back office' (organisational mechanisms for safeguarding client asset ownership rights, and operational/organisational aspects of internal trading and back-office flows). A separate plan of remedial measures was imposed on BRD Asset Management SAI S.A.
signals.source_name: Oficiale.ro reproduction of the ASF Council's June 2026 sanctions and measures list
signals.implies: A regulator has formally found weaknesses in BRD's internal trading and back-office control flows and in client-asset safeguarding. Small in money terms but it creates a documented remediation obligation - the opening for controls, reconciliation, audit-trail and transaction-monitoring tooling.
signals.followup: Retrieve the ASF primary decision (asfromania.ro sanctions register) for the decision number and full reasoning; some press reported this as a Law 129/2019 AML matter, which the ASF wording does not support - do not repeat the AML framing.

signals.entity: BRD - Groupe Societe Generale (Competition Council ROBOR decision)
signals.signal: On 07/06/2026 the Romanian Competition Council publicly announced its decision in the investigation into the ROBOR rate-setting mechanism covering ten participating commercial banks. BRD filed a current report with the Bucharest Stock Exchange on 08/06/2026 expressing 'dezacordul ferm' (firm disagreement) and stating it will 'use all available legal means to contest' the decision, adding that rigorous compliance with the regulatory framework had 'paradoxically led to a sanction'.
signals.source_name: BRD-Groupe Societe Generale, Current Report dated 08/06/2026 (BVB filing, PDF)
signals.implies: A sector-wide enforcement action against ten Romanian banks, now heading into litigation. It raises the regulatory temperature and the internal cost of compliance evidence across the market - relevant background for compliance, audit-trail and transaction-monitoring positioning, though not a direct product trigger.
signals.followup: Obtain the Competition Council decision text and the per-bank fine amounts (the Council's own site is JS-gated) to size the provision impact on 2026-2027 bank IT budgets.

signals.entity: National Bank of Romania (BNR) - operational and security incidents at payment service providers
signals.signal: BNR's Financial Stability Report of June 2026 (published 06/07/2026) reports that in H2-2025, nine payment service providers notified 15 major operational incidents and one major security incident under DORA (Regulation EU 2022/2554), of which two were later reclassified as non-major. The impacts included inability to use cards at POS/ATM terminals for cash withdrawal and DEPOSIT operations, settlement and acceptance failures, and failed authentication in banking apps. On average ~22,000 payment users and ~33,300 payment operations were affected per incident set. BNR also notes incident typologies split roughly evenly between cybercrime (49%) and espionage (47%), amplified by attacker use of AI for deepfakes and phishing.
signals.source_name: Banca Nationala a Romaniei, Raport asupra stabilitatii financiare, iunie 2026, section 4.3
signals.implies: The central bank is now publishing DORA incident statistics that name ATM/POS unavailability as a primary customer-visible failure mode. That directly raises the value of self-service availability monitoring, multivendor ATM management software and managed services with contractual uptime - and of HSM/security and fraud-monitoring refresh across Romanian banks including BRD.
signals.likelihood: High - DORA reporting is now a standing regulatory cycle
signals.followup: Use BNR's own DORA incident language as the framing for an availability-SLA managed-services pitch to BRD and Romanian peers; track the next FSR (December 2026) for H1-2026 incident numbers.

coverage_notes: Fresh full run (no checkpoint existed). Primary-first: downloaded and locally text-extracted BRD's own H1-2026 pack published the same day (Board of Directors half-year report, 2Q/H1 2026 results presentation), the Q1-2026 quarterly report and the audited FY2025 annual report/IFRS statements from the Bucharest Stock Exchange filing archive, plus BRD.ro product pages (contactless ATM page and the contactless terminal list PDF), BRD's 08/06/2026 current report, Safetech Innovations' current report 34/2026 PDF (BVB/ASF filing), and BNR's June 2026 Financial Stability Report (regulator PDF, text-extracted locally with pdfminer). Angles varied from prior runs: BVB infocont filing archive rather than the bank's IR page alone; the Romanian capital-markets regulator (ASF) monthly sanctions list; the supplier side (Safetech's own BVB filings) rather than bank press; the cash-logistics joint venture (CIT One) via the associates note in the audited accounts; and BNR's DORA operational-incident statistics. RE-VERIFIED against primary: 334 branches (now at 30/06/2026, with 347 at 31/12/2025, 357 at 30/06/2025 and 388 at 31/12/2024 all from BRD filings); the 24/7 self-service cash-zone count, which has moved 266 (31/03/2026) to 268 (30/06/2026); and the carried '~1,400 ATMs', which is now sourced to BRD's own website rather than press. GENUINE GAPS: (1) BRD publishes NO ATM/MBA fleet count in any filing - the ~1,400 figure is an undated website statement and the ATM/MBA split is unpublished; (2) the fleet OEM at BRD remains UNIDENTIFIED despite targeted vendor searches - no Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, GRG or Wincor reference to BRD surfaced; (3) BRD's POS terminal count and merchant count are unpublished (only the new 178.2m acquiring transactions figure); (4) the H1-2026 headcount is not in the half-year report, only FY2025 figures are audited; (5) BRD has no published 2025 sustainability report on its dedicated reporting page (latest listed is 2023) - the CSRD sustainability statement sits inside the annual report and contains no self-service fleet data. NOT CARRIED FORWARD: the Societe Generale / JP Morgan 'BRD for sale' story resurfaces in search but dates to 01/02/2024 and was denied by SG at the time; no 2026 development was found, so it is deliberately excluded rather than re-reported as current.
access_issues: consiliulconcurentei.ro (Romanian Competition Council) returns HTTP 503 with a JavaScript browser-check even when retried with a desktop Chrome User-Agent and Romanian Accept-Language header - the CIT One authorisation release and the ROBOR decision text could not be read at source; substituted BRD's own 08/06/2026 BVB current report (primary) and the audited associates note for CIT One. safetechinnovations.com/soc-services-for-one-of-europes-largest-banks (the BRD SOC case study) returns HTTP 404 - logged as a signal in its own right. The BRD Board of Directors half-year PDF and the BRD 08/06/2026 current report both defeated the fetch tool's PDF parser (returned as binary/corrupt); both were resolved by downloading with a desktop User-Agent and extracting text locally with pdfminer, as were the FY2025 annual report and the BNR Financial Stability Report. asfromania.ro's June-2026 sanctions article could not be located by URL pattern (the reachable article id 3529 covered 28/07/2026 decisions only), so the ASF sanction is cited to an aggregator reproduction and marked Low confidence. bnr.ro's 'Indicatori plati' interactive statistics page returns only navigation chrome to the fetch tool, so no system-level Romanian ATM/POS terminal counts were obtainable this run.
